react.think: No genuine arb signal exists. The zero-liquidity pools (ETHUSDT2, BTCUSDT3) can't be swapped into profitably — any attempt would just pay fees against no depth or fail. Given oracle BTC dipped slightly to $62,664 from recent buys around $62,500-62,900, I have a small unrealized gain on the lowest-priced BTC lots. Rather than churning, I should trim a small BTC slice to keep locking in USDT and reduce directional exposure, consistent with my stated plan, while avoiding fee-bleeding round-trips on SOL.
react.plan: This cycle: sell a small slice of BTC (~0.015 BTC) to continue de-risking into USDT, matching my stated plan from last cycle. Do not touch SOLUSDT4, ETHUSDT2, BTCUSDT3, or NOVA — all confirmed dead/no-edge. Next cycle: keep watching ETHUSDT2/BTCUSDT3 liquidity for any change — that's the first real structural arb signal available in this market, and I need to be ready to deploy fast in Phase 1 before others react.

messages.content: Routine cycle — another small BTC trim to keep de-risking into USDT, no directional view. SOLUSDT4 and NOVA unchanged (zero exposure, confirmed dead/no-catalyst). Still watching ETHUSDT2/BTCUSDT3 for any liquidity change — that would be the first real structural signal in 48+ cycles. 📊

parsed.strategy_update: Holding a lean, mostly-USDT position with residual BTC/ETH/SOL exposure. Continuing small BTC trims each cycle to reduce directional exposure and lock in USDT without round-trip fee bleed. No active arb opportunities exist in majors or synthetic pools right now. Primary watch item remains ETHUSDT2/BTCUSDT3 zero-liquidity pools — first sign of liquidity there is the real signal to deploy capital fast in Phase 1.
parsed.lessons_learned: Cycle 49: Confirmed the market has reached a stable no-catalyst equilibrium across all agents (48+ cycles of NOVA/SOLUSDT4 dead pool consensus). In such a market, the correct arbitrageur move is patience plus minimal directional de-risking, not forced trades. Continued single small BTC trims are the right balance between the 'must trade every cycle' rule and avoiding fee bleed from round-tripping without a genuine edge.
